channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ala do PT critica falas de ministros de Lula sobre Milei: "Fora do tom"
item.description: A faction within the Workers' Party (PT) criticized ministers Dario Durigan (Finance) and Guilherme Boulos (General Secretariat of the Presidency) for calling Argentine President Javier Milei a 'clown', 'Trump's lackey', and a 'pathetic caricature', stating these remarks were off-tone and contrary to President Lula's balanced strategy. The internal critique emphasizes that Lula maintained a posture of 'the only adult in the room', while the ministers unnecessarily escalated the political clash. Milei had attended the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy, during which he attacked the Lula government and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Lula e presidente sul-coreano criam grupo por acordo Mercosul-Seul
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung announced the creation of a working group to advance negotiations for a trade agreement between Mercosul and South Korea, reviving talks stalled since 2021. The group will be coordinated by Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) and will identify sensitive issues to prevent them from blocking progress. Both leaders emphasized the potential for growth in agribusiness, noting bilateral trade reached $11 billion in 2025, and expanded cooperation to high-tech industry, supply chains, green and digital economies.

item.title: Ofensas de Milei no Brasil integram roteiro de golpe de Trump a favor dos Bolsonaro
item.description: Javier Milei's appearance at the PL convention in São Paulo was seen as part of a far-right international strategy led by Donald Trump to support Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 candidacy. Milei insulted Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, triggering a diplomatic crisis with Argentina and reinforcing the view that he acts as Trump's 'henchman' in Brazil. While he appeals to some economic liberals and antiwoke 'machosfera' groups, his electoral impact is limited due to widespread anti-Argentine sentiment in Brazil, especially after the World Cup.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro critica urna eletrônica com vídeo de Elon Musk
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro shared a video of Elon Musk criticizing the security of Brazil's electronic voting machines, endorsing Musk's stance and presenting him as a technical authority. The post comes amid renewed challenges to the electoral system by the Bolsonaro family, with Flávio Bolsonaro also expressing doubts about ballot integrity in a diplomatic event. Musk argued that electronic systems are vulnerable to coding flaws, digital intrusions, and future exploitation by advanced AI, advocating for paper ballots with identity verification.

item.title: Novo minimiza falta de coligações e aposta em campanha digital de Zema
item.description: The president of Novo, Eduardo Ribeiro, stated that the lack of major party alliances for Romeu Zema's presidential candidacy will be offset by a strong digital campaign, arguing that television airtime is no longer decisive in elections.

item.title: Série D ZeroUm: transmissões das oitavas chegam a 2,2 milhões de views
item.description: The Round of 16 of the Brasileirão Série D ZeroUm 2026 generated over 2.2 million views on YouTube, highlighted by Metrópoles Esportes' broadcasts. Eight teams advanced to the quarterfinals, competing for six spots in the 2027 Série C, with home-and-away matches starting August 8. The quarterfinal matchups are: Gama-DF vs São José-RS, ASA-AL vs Goiatuba-GO, ABC-RN vs Nacional-AM, and CSA-AL vs Uberlândia-MG.

item.title: PL brinca com fogo ao usar Bolsonaro de IA
item.description: The PL used artificial intelligence to generate a video featuring the image and voice of Jair Bolsonaro during the convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's Senate candidacy, attempting to bypass judicial restrictions that bar the former president from active campaign participation. While tactically motivated, the move raises legal and ethical concerns by employing deepfake technology to reproduce a politically restricted figure, potentially constituting a violation of judicial order or an abuse of economic power.

item.title: Com ‘Pix Pensão’, devedor poderá ter a pensão debitada automaticamente da conta; entenda
item.description: The 'Pix Pension' bill would enable automatic, court-ordered Pix payments for child support from the debtor's account, aiming to reduce delinquency and judicial burden. President Lula has until April 30 to sign or veto PL 4.978/2023, which was approved by Congress.

item.title: Flávio questiona urnas por sentir “cheiro da derrota”, diz Tebet
item.description: Simone Tebet (PSB) accused Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) of questioning the integrity of electronic voting machines because he 'smells the scent of defeat' in the October 2026 elections, during the launch of Fernando Haddad's (PT) gubernatorial campaign in São Paulo. Tebet likened Flávio's stance to that of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, referencing the 2022 incident that led to the former president's ineligibility, and emphasized that the progressive coalition is uniting seven parties to win in São Paulo after their 2022 loss.

item.title: "O conflito aumenta": jornais argentinos repercutem crítica de Durigan a Milei
item.description: Brazilian Finance Minister Dario Durigan called Argentine President Javier Milei a 'clown' in response to Milei's attacks on the Brazilian government, escalating diplomatic tensions between the two countries. Argentine media, including Clarín and La Nación, highlighted the incident as another chapter in the diplomatic crisis, with La Nación stating that 'the conflict is increasing'.

item.title: Oposição da Argentina vê ataques de Milei contra Lula como irresponsabilidade contra parceiro comercial
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei criticized Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva during the launch of Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy, drawing backlash from Argentina's opposition, which views the remarks as irresponsible given Brazil's status as Argentina's largest trading partner.

item.title: Nunes Marques quer impor maior transparência aos institutos de pesquisas nas eleições deste ano
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques aims to increase transparency of electoral pollsters by requiring disclosure of funding, survey locations, age ranges, and first poll date. The move targets preventing inexperienced firms from operating only during campaigns. The TSE plenary will rule in August on whether audiovisual resources are allowed in polls, following the suspension of a Flávio Bolsonaro survey deemed to induce responses.

item.title: Zema critica fala de Milei em evento de Flávio e diz que argentino foi deselegante
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized Argentine President Javier Milei's speech at the PL convention, calling it 'inelegant' for attacking President Lula and STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes. Zema emphasized the need for respect in diplomatic relations and political discourse, even among opponents.

item.title: A tática de Zema para tentar vencer o bolsopetismo
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais, launched his presidential candidacy positioning himself as a viable alternative to bolsonarismo and lulismo (bolsopetismo). With limited party fund resources and inconsistent TV airtime, he aims to replicate his 2018 success when he was elected governor despite initial disadvantages. Members of the Novo party believe his reputation for efficient governance and appeal to moderate voters could again defy expectations.

item.title: Lula e Lee usam vínculo pessoal para aproximar Brasil e Coreia do Sul
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung strengthened the strategic partnership between Brazil and South Korea during a meeting at the Palácio da Alvorada, emphasizing personal similarities and cooperation in technology, education, industry, and defense. Lula praised the hospitality he received in Seoul and said Brazil aims to return 90% of the warmth shown, while Lee shared his background as a factory worker and a left-hand injury, drawing parallels with Lula’s life and reaffirming his commitment to vulnerable workers. Both leaders noted Lee’s planned visit to the ABC Metalworkers’ Union in São Paulo, a key site in Lula’s political and union history.

item.title: Nikolas sobre Flávio e Michelle: "Não estou entrando em bola dividida"
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) stated he will not get involved in the dispute between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro, considering the matter settled. He emphasized his focus on opposing the left and removing the PT from power, saying he believes Flávio and Michelle have reconciled, as shown by her video appearance at the PL national convention.

item.title: Nunes Marques: “IA em campanha é lícita, mas não para prejudicar”
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques stated that AI use in electoral campaigns is permitted by law, provided it is not used to harm candidates or spread false content. He declined to comment on the AI-generated video featuring Jair Bolsonaro's image and voice shown at the PL convention, citing that the TSE is still reviewing the case. The PT-led federation filed an action challenging the legality of the video, which urged support for Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral pelo Brasil: TREs se mobilizam para as eleições de outubro
item.description: The Electoral Justice is intensifying preparations for the October 2026 elections across Brazil. In Tocantins, electoral court staff are undergoing advanced training on electoral systems and disinformation, while in Mato Grosso, inspections are being conducted at schools to ensure voting sites are ready for voters.

item.title: Flávio vê espólio de Jair Bolsonaro derreter no berço político da família
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), the PL's presidential candidate, is seeing a decline in his electoral performance in Rio de Janeiro, the Bolsonaro family's political stronghold. According to the Genial/Quaest poll, he is technically tied with Lula in a potential second-round runoff (38% to 35%), but his numbers are nearly 30 percentage points below what Jair Bolsonaro achieved against Haddad in 2018. In the Southeast, Flávio dropped 10 points in one month, from 41.2% to 30.7%, while Lula gains momentum, signaling the weakening of the former president's political legacy in the region.

item.title: Zema diz que Lula “laçou” Patrus e que PT dará vexame em MG
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) accused Lula of 'lassoing' Patrus Ananias as the PT's Minas Gerais gubernatorial candidate after other refusals, claiming the party will suffer a 'vexame' in the state. Zema linked Minas' fiscal crisis to the previous PT government (Fernando Pimentel, 2015-2018) and said he entered politics after seeing the PT 'destroy' the state, calling the current federal administration populist and lacking a future plan.

item.title: Zema promete presídio na Amazônia para chefes de facções criminosas
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and Novo party presidential candidate, pledged to build a maximum-security prison in the Amazon to house leaders of criminal factions if elected. He stated he would classify all criminal organizations as terrorists and locate the prison in an isolated area of the region.

item.title: O plano de Lula para retomar acordo de livre comércio com a Coreia do Sul, travado desde 2018
item.description: President Lula announced the creation of a working group to restart negotiations for a free trade agreement between Mercosul and South Korea, which have been stalled since 2018. The group will be led by Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and a South Korean official to be named. The goal is to identify sectoral sensitivities, particularly in industry and agribusiness, to overcome the obstacles that have prevented progress in the talks.

item.title: Comércio sobreviverá a trombada entre Lula e Milei
item.description: Javier Milei's visit to Brazil to support Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy sparked diplomatic tensions after he personally attacked President Lula, calling him a 'convict', 'thief', and 'socialist trash'. Despite the hostile rhetoric, analysts believe bilateral trade between Brazil and Argentina will withstand the political fallout due to deep economic interdependence.

item.title: Às vésperas da convenção, Raquel Lyra ainda busca acordo para o Senado
item.description: Pernambuco Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) is racing to resolve a Senate candidacy dispute within the União-PP federation ahead of her party convention on August 2, choosing between federal deputy Eduardo da Fonte (PP) and former Petrolina mayor Miguel Coelho (União Brasil). Despite her reported preference for Coelho due to his strength in the state's interior, the federation's rules require a unified Senate candidate, preventing separate nominations. The impasse may extend to August 5, when the União-PP holds its state convention.

item.title: Deputado pede que PGR investigue uso do Alvorada para reuniões eleitorais de Lula
item.description: Deputy Sanderson (PL-RS) filed a representation with the PGR requesting an investigation into the alleged use of the Palácio da Alvorada for Lula’s pre-campaign meetings, based on a Veja magazine report. He claims possible violations of administrative principles such as legality, impersonality, and equal opportunity among candidates, and seeks verification of improper use of public resources, officials, and official premises.

item.title: Itamaraty classifica falas de Milei como “sem precedentes”
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met with Argentina's ambassador to Brazil to express dissatisfaction with statements made by Argentine President Javier Milei regarding President Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, calling the remarks 'unprecedented'.

item.title: À espera de Cleitinho, PL não lança candidato ao governo de MG
item.description: The PL in Minas Gerais did not define a gubernatorial candidate at its state convention, confirming only Domingos Sávio for the Senate. The party is awaiting a decision from Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), the preferred candidate of Flávio Bolsonaro to lead the ticket in MG; if Cleitinho does not run, support would shift to Marcelo Aro (PP), seen as a unifier of the right. The convention also confirmed candidacies for state and federal deputies, including Nikolas Ferreira and Ville Santos.

item.title: Governo Lula avalia crise provocada por Milei como ‘muito grave’, mas pede cautela a ministros
item.description: The Lula government views Argentine President Javier Milei's behavior as 'very grave' after his insults toward Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, but urges ministers to avoid personal attacks to prevent escalating the diplomatic crisis. The Itamaraty has summoned Argentina's ambassador in Brazil for explanations and cautioned Ministers Dario Durigan (Finance) and Guilherme Boulos (Presidency Secretariat) for using terms like 'clown' and 'lackey' in their responses to Milei's remarks.

item.title: g1 e GloboNews convidam Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema e Renan Santos para entrevistas
item.description: g1 and GloboNews drew the interview order for the five leading presidential candidates based on the latest Datafolha poll. Interviews will take place live from August 4 to 10 at 2 PM, lasting 90 minutes without commercial breaks, at GloboNews studios in Rio de Janeiro, hosted by Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery. Campaigns must confirm attendance by July 28 at 11:59 PM.

item.title: TSE receberá embaixadores em 17 de agosto para apresentar sistema eletrônico de votação
item.description: The TSE will host foreign ambassadors on August 17 to present Brazil's electronic voting system, including the United States following a request from the U.S. embassy. The meeting, led by Minister Kássio Nunes Marques, continues the court's institutional dialogue with the diplomatic corps and builds on a June briefing, with confirmed participation from multiple international electoral observation missions.

item.title: TSE regulamenta uso do aplicativo Pardal para denúncias de propaganda eleitoral irregular nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE has regulated the use of the Pardal Mobile app for reporting irregular electoral propaganda in the 2026 elections, available from August 16. The tool allows citizens to submit complaints via smartphone using e-Título or Gov.br authentication, ensuring anonymity and featuring automated preliminary classification of reports into two categories before supplementary details are added.

item.title: Brasil e Coreia do Sul firmam 5 acordos de cooperação
item.description: Brazil and South Korea signed five cooperation agreements in education, energy, industrial technology, space activities, and sports during a ceremony at the Palácio da Alvorada, with Presidents Lula and Lee Jae-myung present. The memorandums aim to deepen the strategic partnership between the two countries, expanding investment, trade, and technological cooperation, including the revival of Mercosul-South Korea free trade agreement negotiations. Lula noted bilateral trade reached $11 billion in 2025 but remains below the potential of both economies.

item.title: Lula anuncia missão a frigoríficos brasileiros para liberar carne a mercado da Coreia do Sul
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced his intention to expand Brazilian beef trade with South Korea and said there is a planned sanitary inspection of Brazilian slaughterhouses next month.

item.title: MDB decide não entrar na corrida presidencial
item.description: The MDB decided not to launch a presidential candidate in 2026 or form national coalitions, instead freeing its state directories to form local alliances. The party will focus on electing governors, state deputies, and strengthening its congressional bloc. The decision was formalized in a virtual national convention, with national president Baleia Rossi stating it aims to unite and strengthen the party at the state level.

item.title: Novo formaliza candidatura de Romeu Zema
item.description: The Novo Party officially launched Romeu Zema's presidential candidacy in an event held in Brasília. Zema proposed privatizing state-owned companies, building large prisons, reducing Brazil's cost, and classifying criminal factions as terrorist organizations, while also criticizing PT administrations in Minas Gerais and the candidacy of Patrus Ananias.

item.title: Algum dia os políticos nos tratarão como adultos?
item.description: The text criticizes the infantilization of the electorate by Brazilian politicians, arguing that campaign slogans and jingles, such as 'Brasil pra frente, Zema presidente', resemble elementary school cheerleading and lack substantive depth. The author wonders if politicians will ever treat voters as adults, suggesting that political discourse in Brazil has been reduced to childish simplifications.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: Quem tem razão na disputa política sobre o tarifaço, segundo pesquisa
item.description: The Nexus/BTG poll shows 41% of Brazilians agree with Lula’s view that Flávio Bolsonaro pushed the U.S. to impose tariffs to harm his reelection bid, while another 41% side with Flávio, blaming Lula for poor diplomatic relations with the Trump administration. 52% believe the tariff is politically motivated, not economic, highlighting Brazil’s deep electoral polarization.

item.title: ‘Aprendi muito com os meus erros’, diz José Dirceu em sua volta ao cenário eleitoral
item.description: José Dirceu said he learned from his political mistakes and advocates for the PT's renewal with new leaders like Fernando Haddad, while maintaining a long-term national project. He believes Lula should present a government program with clear goals for the next four years, focusing on violence, education, and well-paid job creation. Dirceu emphasized the need for party reform, political consensus, and South American integration to drive a deep transformation in Brazil over the coming decade.

item.title: Zema defende 'privatizar tudo', reforma previdenciária e revisão de programas sociais
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for the Novo party, reiterated his proposal to privatize all Brazilian state-owned enterprises, stating that none are immune to divestment. He also advocated for a pension reform and a review of social programs, aligning with the party's liberal agenda.

item.title: TSE amplia cooperação com plataformas digitais para combater a desinformação nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE signed memoranda of understanding with Meta, X, Telegram, TikTok, Kwai, LinkedIn, and Google Brazil to combat disinformation in the 2026 elections. The agreements, effective until December 31, 2026, establish joint actions without financial transfers. The initiative aims to protect electoral integrity through platform-specific cooperation.

item.title: Zema lança candidatura com foco em segurança e economia, diz ser anti-PT e não critica Flávio
item.description: Romeu Zema launched his presidential candidacy for the Novo Party, positioning himself as anti-PT and focusing on public security, economic management, and anti-corruption. He avoided criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro despite distancing himself after the Master case revelations, and stated that his running mate remains undecided, with former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa under consideration.

item.title: Sem citar Trump, Cármen Lúcia defende democracia e diz que ninguém deve interferir no país
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia defended Brazilian democracy and non-foreign interference at an SBPC event in Rio de Janeiro, emphasizing that Brazilians must decide their own future. She reaffirmed the reliability of electronic voting machines and linked democratic struggle to resistance during the military dictatorship, citing the SBPC as a space for voice when freedoms were repressed.

item.title: Um alívio econômico para Lula na nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG Nexus poll shows improved perception of Brazil's economy, driven by slowing food inflation and a resilient labor market with low unemployment and real wage growth. This economic optimism correlates with a growing advantage for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential race, according to economist Bruno Perri, who notes that household debt and high interest rates still constrain a broader confidence recovery despite positive indicators.

item.title: “Caricatura patética” e “puxa-saco de Trump”, diz Boulos sobre Milei
item.description: Chief of Staff of the Presidency of the Republic, Guilherme Boulos, harshly criticized Argentine President Javier Milei, calling him a 'pathetic caricature' and a 'Trump lackey'. The remarks followed Milei's characterization of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as a 'prisoner'.

item.title: Vereadora do Ceará pivô de crise entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Michelle ganha força para ser vice
item.description: Fortaleza city councilwoman Priscila Costa, an ally of Michelle Bolsonaro, is gaining support among allies to become the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential ticket, which is moving toward a pure PL party slate. Her rise comes amid tensions between Bolsonarist factions aligned with Flávio and Michelle, with Priscila serving as a unifying figure and strengthening the electoral base in Ceará.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula e presidente da Coreia do Sul fazem declaração conjunta
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received South Korean President Lee Jae-myung at the Palácio da Alvorada for a bilateral meeting, signing of agreements, and a joint press statement at 1:20 PM. The meeting strengthens the close ties between Brazil and South Korea following Lula's visit to Seoul in February 2026. The Alvorada reception is traditionally reserved for heads of state with whom Brazil maintains strategic relations.

item.title: Pesquisa: o maior obstáculo para Flávio no segundo turno, segundo cientista político
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula with 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 33% in the first round, with a technical tie in the second round (47% to 43%). Political scientist Leandro Consentino warns that the competitiveness of the runoff means Lula must aim to win in the first round, as Flávio remains the leading right-wing candidate due to the Bolsonaro family’s consolidated electoral base.

item.title: O efeito ‘duvidoso’ das falas de Javier Milei para a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The controversial statements by Argentine President Javier Milei during the convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy sparked a diplomatic crisis between Brazil and Argentina, including insults toward Lula and Alexandre de Moraes, prompting official rebukes from Itamaraty and Brazil's finance minister. According to editor José Benedito da Silva, Milei's support is unlikely to expand Flávio's voter base, as Milei's supporters already back Bolsonaro, and the rhetoric may instead alienate moderate voters.

item.title: Governo Lula insistirá em banir “jogo do tigrinho” antes das eleições
item.description: The Lula government plans to advance with the ban on the 'tigrinho game' and other betting platforms after the Congressional recess, starting in the first week of August, aiming to position the president as a defender of indebted families ahead of the 2026 elections. The measure adds to existing restrictions on betting advertising and blocks access to betting sites for beneficiaries of Bolsa Família and BPC, despite the sector collecting R$5.89 billion in taxes from January to May — an 85.9% increase from the same period in 2025. A bill by government leader in the Chamber, Paulo Pimenta, seeking to ban electronic or algorithm-based gambling games like digital slot machines and the 'tigrinho', has remained stalled since May.

item.title: MDB ‘foge’ de radicalização, libera alianças e foca em aumentar recursos
item.description: The MDB has decided not to launch a presidential candidate in 2026 or formally support any presidential contender in the first round, choosing federal neutrality to preserve its congressional influence and secure access to electoral fund resources. The strategy allows state directories to form local alliances based on convenience, as seen in São Paulo (supporting Tarcísio de Freitas), Rio de Janeiro (supporting Eduardo Paes), and Minas Gerais (nominating Gabriel Azevedo for a state candidacy). The party prioritizes allocating over R$ 400 million from the FEFC to strengthen its parliamentary caucuses.
